avcodec/bsf/extract_extradata: add support for LCEVC

fix_commit_message:
avcodec/bsf/extract_extradata: Check that block_size is not negative

Fixes: out of array access
Fixes: 490576036/clusterfuzz-testcase-minimized-ffmpeg_BSF_EXTRACT_EXTRADATA_fuzzer-4605696279904256

Found-by: continuous fuzzing process https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/master/projects/ffmpeg
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 248b481c337d on top of intro 3dba9eb80663 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (IntegerOverflow): The LCEVC extradata extraction code in libavcodec/bsf/extract_extradata.c parses an enhancement-layer NALU payload size using a multi-byte variable-length encoding (get_mb, which returns up to a 64-bit value truncated by up to 10 iterations of 7-bit groups). This value is stored in a plain 32-bit signed int (payload_size) and then added to a bit offset to compute block_size. Because payload_size can be very large (attacker controlled via crafted bitstream), the addition can overflow a signed int, producing a negative block_size. The existing bounds check 'block_size >= bytestream2_get_bytes_left(&gbc)' does not reject negative values, so processing continues and block_size/raw_block_size (negative or wrapped) is used to compute buffer offsets and drive bytestream2_put_buffer/bytestream2_skip calls, resulting in an out-of-bounds memory access as detected by OSS-Fuzz. Root cause: The code introduced in the LCEVC extradata support used a 32-bit signed int to hold a payload size read via a multi-byte/variable length decoder (get_mb, uint64_t) without validating that the value fits within range before using it in pointer/length arithmetic, allowing signed integer overflow and a negative computed block_size to bypass the sanity check that only guarded against overly large (not negative) sizes.
